meta_description_en: Letters section in Outlet #129: Arnold Yates asks about Citizen 120-D printer support and disassembling Icon Graphic 128, Brian Cavers responds, and Colin Bibby writes in.
meta_description_ru: Рубрика писем Outlet #129: вопросы Arnold Yates о выводе на принтер Citizen 120-D и дизассемблировании Icon Graphic 128, ответ Brian Cavers и письмо Colin Bibby.

May,1998   No.129   Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 Arnold Yates.........03    05

 Colin Bibby..........07    10

 Bernadette Dowsland..12    14

 Harvey Milner........17    18

 J. Littlemore........19    22

 Colin Bibby..........24    32

 Miles Kinloch........36    39

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: William Arnold Yates,LANCS


Dear Chezron,

I wonder if anyone can help me?
I have the program Icon Graphic
128 on a disc,What I am looking
for is the original that is on
cassette. Also how can I make it
print out on a Citizen 120-D? It
will print out on a ZX printer
or an Alphacom 32 but I can't
use a Plus D interface and disc
drive in conjuction with the ZX
printer. Yes, I know about the
Twoface but have you tried to
get one? But even with the Two-
face it won't print out the full
width of the Citizen printer -
only ZX width.


Can anyone tell me how to break
in to machine code and how to
change the code to allow me to
use a full size printer? I think
I know that you have to use a
disassembler to get in to it but
how to do this I just don't
know. So if anyone can help
please let me know what I need
and how to go about it.

Any help will be welcome so
please someone, put me out of my
misery and help me out.

        Yours sincerely,

         Arnold Yates

Brian Cavers to Arnold Yates


What kind of program is Icon
Graphic 128? It's not a name I
know. If it is a graphics/text
editor maybe you would be better
off with WORDMASTER.

It is not an easy matter to dis-
assemble and alter machine code.
You cannot simply get a disass-
embler, learn a few rules, and
then go ahead. It is much more
difficult than changing BASIC
which itself can be very hard at
times. There is a disassembler
in OUTLET 82 called TOPS but you
need to be able to program in
machine code to understand what
to do with it.


Furthermore, it may not be easy,
or even possible to change the
program you describe depending
on how it creates the 32 column
material. It might be feasible
to redirect it to a full size
printer but more difficult to
change the width. It might print
Sinclair defined graphics on a
ZX printer but this would need a
complete re-write to emulate on
a full-size printer.

I'm a little puzzled that it is
called '128', implying that it
was created for the 128K Spect-
rum; after all, the ZX printer
will not run in 128K mode any-
way. How do you know that it is
in machine code; perhaps it was
written in BASIC.
                         Brian

From: Colin Bibby


     GREAT, ANOTHER OUTLET.
        LUV IT TO BITS.

BUT...

There are a few too many bits
and pieces floating around
scattered on floors tables and
chairs at my home at present
while attempts to tidy up my
ZXing exercises and Outlets
continue to built to great
heights.

    MOUNTAIN  CLIMBING  WASN'T
    ENVISAGED  WHEN I  STARTED
    MY ZXING A COUPLE OF YEARS
              AGO!


But please don't let all that
stop you from sending me my
regular copy of Outlet.


Now for yet another question
relating to "BFORMAT.BAS" which
might also please other Outlet
readers to discover. This is the
3.5" "B" drive formatter for the
+3 available from Chezron. When
loaded, the proggy asks...

ALTERNATING or SUCCESSIVE SIDES
A/S (DEFAULT = S). HIT ENTER FOR
DEFAULT VALUES.

Next comes:-

NO. OF DIRECTORY ENTRIES 128/256
(DEFAULT 128)?


In each of the above modes I
always simply ENTER the default
values set, and it works to
provide 710K per 3.5" disc. But
what do all these A/S and
128/256 relate to? Seems stupid,
or is it me?

Thanks for the fab zine everyone

           C. Bibby


Brian Cavers to Colin Bibby

The tracks on a double-sided
disk may be formatted and numb-
ered in sequence from the start
of side A to the end of Side A
and then from the start of Side
B to the end of Side B. This is
the 'SUCCESSIVE SIDES' method.

Alternatively, the disk may be
formatted by formatting Track 0
on Side A then Track 0 on Side B
then Track 1 on Side A then
Track 1 on Side B and so on to
the final tracks on each side.
This is the 'ALTERNATE SIDES'
method. The drive has two heads,
one on each side, so it does not
have to physically move back and
forth between sides.


Which is best? I doubt there is
any significant difference so
don't worry about it but just
accept the default(unless anyone
else knows better?)

The number of directory entries
is a different matter. If you
choose 256 you will be able to
save more files on the disk (128
more in fact!) but there will be
slightly less overall room on
the disk (706K).This is suitable
for disks where you want to save
the maximum number of very small
files, eg, say 200 odd 2K text
files.But where 128 is more than
enough files of average size
that you want to store then you
might as well have the extra 4K
of space and format to 710K.
                         Brian

      Bernadette Dowsland
        26 Elsie Street
             Goole
         East Yorkshire
            DN14 6DU

Dear Outlet Readers,

I would like to let you all know
that I have recently acquired a
Romantic Robot Digitiser.

If anyone would like any artwork
putting on the spectrum then
drop me a line at my above addr-
ess. My rates are low, as long
as I cover my costs I am happy.

I don't have a video camera at
present so all material must be
sent as VHS or Beta video cass-
ette.

Cartoons usually come out best.
Line drawing are ideal but they
must only occupy about 2/3rds of
the TV screen both length and
breadth wise.

Faces come out best if videoed
against a white background and
as mentioned above, filling
2/3rd's of the screen.

In addition to any digitizing
done to order all customers will
get at least one disc of cartoon
digitized characters all ready
for you to colour in via your
favourite art package.

All formats are supported, Opus,
+D,+3 (A and B drive)
                      Bernadette


Brian to Bernadette Dowsland

I wanted one of those digitizers
for years but never did get one
for the Spectrum. Later I bought
a PC one and I can also use this
for the Spectrum by converting
to black and white and transf-
erring it. This is how I do the
animations I sometimes put into
OUTLET.

You can have a lot of fun with a
digitizer and especially animat-
ions.To do an animation you need
some sort of cyclic motion so it
repeats: Bugs Bunny being chased
by Yosemite Sam for instance. It
is important that the cycle is
completed in no more than say, 8
to 12 frames (depending on how
complex).

It is also important that the
final frame 'matches' to the
first frame to produce the cycle
of frames. Often you need to
touch up the frames in an art
package. It can be very labour
intensive!

For instance, the legs and arms
of Yosemite Sam chasing Bugs
Bunny may link correctly from
the final frame to the first but
the background may suddenly jerk
to a new scene so has to be man-
ually erased bit by bit to leave
just the figures. Sometimes you
can replace that background by
some simple lines to help with
the illusion of movement (like
the pavement in MR NUMO in OUT-
LET 100.


While testing, one can simply
load the screens one by one from
disk in a loop.

When you have your frames you
need to compress them. I use the
PICPACKER from OUTLET 35.

The compressed frames need to be
all loaded into memory in sequ-
ence and their start addresses
noted. The whole lot are then
resaved as one big block of code
for convenience.

If you feel like having a go you
can nick the BASIC from one of
the previous animations as a
template if you want. They're
good fun but do take time and a
lot of patience!
                       Brian

From: Harvey Milner,
email: harvey.milner@virgin.net

Ron,

Just a question about printing
from the Outlet disk:why does it
only print in a single column
and in the middle of a page? Is
it not possible to print across
the page? If so, how is this
done?  Excellent magazine by the
way - hope it keeps going. I am
showing my ignorance probably
but if you don't ask you stay
ignorant.

          Regards,

                   Harvey


Brian Cavers to Harvey Milner

The OUTLET text is formatted to
the 32 columns of the Spectrum
screen and the printout is just
the same text sent to a printer
instead of the screen. To print
out a complete document use our
TABLOID option which prints out
like a newspaper.

Alternatively, use COL80 PLUS
from OUTLET 24.

                  Brian

From: J. Littlemore, FLINTS






Dear Brian,

I sent you a disk late January
stating that I now have a 3.5"
disk drive as B drive on my +3
and would like any future OUT-
LETS in this format for +3. I
received the Feb outlet No.126
on 3" disk and then I received
my disk back from you. Unfortun-
ately, when I inserted the 126
disk in drive A it would not
load.I have tried previous disks
with the same result.


What I get when I insert the
disk and press ENTER on the
loader menu,after some time is:-

Insert tape and press PLAY To
cancel - press BREAK twice.

If I go into +3 mode and type
CAT I get:-

Drive A : track 0, sector 0,
missing address mark. Retry
Ignore or Cancel

If then I press SPACE once I
get:-

Missing address mark,0:1

I changed the drive belt for a
new one in case it was that but
it made no difference.

I have just received OUTLET
No.127 again on 3" disk and I
think that a reply to my disk I
sent you is on one of these last
two. Can I get them changed for
3.5" mode ones so I can look at
them?

I am desperate to get my 3" A
drive working again as I have so
much on these disks that are im-
portant to me as well as all my
OUTLET ones. And can you please
forward future OUTLETs on +3
3.5" disks. Thank You.

I'm lucky I copied my Tasword
onto 3.5 disk.
        Yours Sincerly,

         J. LITTLEMORE

Brian Cavers to J. Littlemore

First, apologies for sending the
wrong version. I think this was
partly due to your letter being
on a disk that Ron can't print
so it was passed to me and by
the time a printed copy got back
to him from me it was too late
for one issue and somehow got
overlooked for the next. Hope-
fully all should now be correct.

If you're sure it's not the belt
then the only solution I can
think of is to look out for a
secondhand Plus 3. It is not
worth paying for a repair even
if you can find someone to do it
I don't think as a Plus 3 is
only worth about `15 or `20.


The trouble is, most secondhand
Spectrums come with loads of
extra bits thus bumping up the
price. However, it must be so
hard to sell off one now that I
would have thought anyone would
be glad of `20 for the Plus 3
alone.

Colin Bibby has a new advert in
OUTBOARD this month which does
mention a second Plus 3 "for
spares". If you contact him it
may be that the drive is OK.

I see another in there from
Arnold Yates with various Spec-
trums including a Plus 3 with a
"make me an offer". Sounds good!

                   Brian

From: Colin Bibby

     OUTLET... Aint it great?
           ZXing too.

I'm going to offer an autobooter
for the "B" drive on the +3.
Before doing so please excuse my
rabbit concerning a late arrived
+3 with gismo's and gadgets. My
mind is presently overflowing
with Outlets because I bought a
+3 plus discs as advertised in
Outboard.

It seems Mr. Castle the previous
owner, has since moved over to a
modern pc therefore his Outlet's
collection and systems are now
owned by myself for the time
being.


I say for the time being because
having now copied the Outlets to
3.5", it will please me to clear
it all again for a reduced price
to anyone interested.

[THIS WOULD BE AN INFRINGEMENT
OF COPYRIGHT!SEE MY REPLY-BRIAN]

With the lot came a modem plus a
fixit board which allows modem
to +3. All rather complicated to
detail here, if anyone can write
details via Outlet for me to
consider making use of the modem
then please do help. I find this
modem quite an interesting gismo
but can it do anything for me?
I think these thingies need to
SHAKE HANDS so to speak but my
knowledge of such technology is
about zero rated.

I'm sure your words will be an
interesting read for other fans
as well as myself.


These Outlets cover a period of
years going back approx ten so
it seems my reading and catching
up here will take me quite a few
months at least.


Having glanced through some I
found a fab FILE CARD system on
number 48. This program almost
blew my old braincells to pieces
because I had been looking for a
similar prog for quite some time
instead of scatterd Tas files
and scraps of paper littering
floors and tabletops.


I found that although this prog
claims 40 cards per A/Z drawer,
(1040 cards max) it allows 35 on
our 710K disc per A/Z drawer
leaving just 28K FREE.So I think
it was probably wrote primarily
for +D which as I understand it
can format 3.5" to 800K. I'm
sure Chezron will be pleased to
distribute this prog to anyone
on request. It's a fab utility
for records filing. Extremely
user friendly too.

          AUTO BOOTER...

Ever since fitting a 3.5" 1.44M
drive to my  +3  it has remained
something of an ordeal loading a
program digit by digit via one
finger jabbing of the qwerty for
drive "B".

Brian's suggestion of:-

10 LOAD "B:":SAVE"B:":LOAD"DISK"

which autoboots the "B" drive
works perfectly. It needs a file
in the "B" drive called "DISK" .

I remained puzzled by that :-

   SAVE "B:" in line 10 above

so tried it without SAVE "B:" .
It works fine  Brian. But if for
some reason it's wise to include
SAVE "B:" then please let me
know.

In addition to the above I have
only recently come up with the
following which is a very rapid
"B" autobooter....

Many of my discs have over ten
programs stored so I wanted a
proggy other than DISK/ADMIN
which would provide me with the
prog list only then offer the
simple single key fast windows
style function. In other words.
Save the line 10 above on a
spare 3" disc. An odd disc with
faulty sectors should suit this
job very well.

As Brian stated, this autobooter
can also be left in the 3" drive
for permanent "B" access via the
enter key.

My new bit came from Page 72 in
the +3 manual concerning DATA.
I'm going to  keep this as brief
as possible but do write through
Outlet for further info if req..

Let's assume you want to gain
access to a disc in the B drive
containing just three programs.

These might be named "ONE" "TWO"
and "THREE" My program to gain
instant access to any of these
programs would be wrote as
follows:-


10 FOR a=1 TO 3
20 READ n$
30 PRINT n$
40 DATA "1 = ONE" , "2 = TWO" ,
     "3 = THREE"
50 NEXT a
60 INPUT "ENTER CHOICE 1 TO 3",z
70 IF z=1 THEN LOAD "ONE"
80 IF z=2 THEN LOAD "TWO"
90 IF z=3 THEN LOAD "THREE"


To save the above onto any disc
do remember to include the line
number 10 for it to autoboot as
follows:-

       SAVE "DISK" LINE 10

Including LINE  10 prevents from
having to type RUN when loaded.

No doubt many softwares do exist
already to offer this function
but theres still a fascination
in writing ones own tailored for
individual needs now and again.

I noticed on OUTLET 39 an 800K
formatter for the +3 B drive. It
didn't function on mine. Any
hints?
                   Colin Bibby

Brian Cavers to Colin Bibby

First, I must point out that it
is AN INFRINGEMENT OF COPYRIGHT
to copy OUTLET disks and sell
either the originals OR the
copies! It is technically ill-
egal to make ANY copies of OUT-
LET but we permit readers to
make copies for their own use
such as for backup or onto a
different system.

You should NEVER sell or even
give away copies of OUTLET. The
odd one to a friend as a sample
to entice them to join is OK but
should not be repeated.

It is OK to sell as secondhand
ORIGINALS of OUTLET SO LONG AS
YOU DO NOT KEEP COPIES.

I'm sure your intentions were
innocent but if you think about
it you can see how soon we would
be out of business if everyone
did it! We'd only need to sell
one OUTLET a month and it could
be passed around to everyone,
each of whom could keep a copy!
Of course, the next month there
would be no OUTLETs at all!

We're well aware that we are
ripped off left,right and centre
and ultimately there is not much
we can do about it but we are
certainly not going to help by
permitting adverts in OUTBOARD!
I have therefore removed that
part of your advert pertaining
to OUTLETs and trust you will
not sell them unless you first
erase your copies.

I should add that MANY items in
OUTLET are public domain or what
we call FREEWARE. These individ-
ual programs may be copied,sold,
or given away to your heart's
content! Items NOT so marked are
copyright and must not be passed
on or sold to others.

Regarding the FILECARD program,
your comment that"I'm sure Chez-
ron will be pleased to distrib-
ute this program to anyone on
request" implies that we will
just send a copy to anyone for
free! Sorry! Anyone wanting the
program must buy OUTLET 48. Yes,
I know how mercenary it sounds
but although OUTLET makes no
profit now we do need to cover
all sorts of costs to keep it
going.

Plus 3 DOS does not provide a
single 'current drive' feature
like the Plus D or Disciple but
splits it between 'current drive
for reading' and 'current drive
for writing'.The SAVE "B:"that I
recommended makes sure that B is
current for writing too. If you
want to be sure all programs
will work fully on Drive B - and
exclusively on B - then you need
the SAVE "B:". Otherwise,a prog-
ram saving data may unexpectedly
save to Drive A. That might be
what you want in some cases but
in general if you want to switch
to using B as the current drive
you need both LOAD "B:" and SAVE
"B:".
                     Brian.

From: Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

Dear Brian,

I read your letter about tube
ageing, and thought I might be
able to throw a little light on
the problem (no pun intended).
The symptoms of low brightness
and poor focus are caused by the
gradual build-up of impurities
on the cathode, and it is this
which reduces its ability to
emit electrons.

A partial cure can be to run the
tube heaters for several minutes
at a higher than normal voltage,
as the increased temperature
then 'boils off' some of the
contaminants, exposing a fresh
layer of emissive material.

This can give a temporary new
lease of life to a tube that is
on its 'last legs', but needs to
be carried out under very strict
conditions to avoid unnecessary
strain on the heaters.

In the earlier days of televis-
ion servicing, this technique
used to be fairly common, as it
was cost-effective to defer the
(considerable) expense of tube
replacement. Nowadays, however,
it's probably more economical to
buy a new set, so I don't know
if the practice is still as
widespread.

I came across a servicing manual
(Newnes TV & Video Engineers'
Pocket Book) that describes the


tube rejuvenation process more
fully: while over-running the
heaters for several seconds, a
positive voltage should also be
applied to the grid, to attract
the oxides away from the
cathode.

              Best wishes,


             Miles Kinloch

Brian Cavers to Miles Kinloch

Many thanks, Miles. Too advanced
for me to try but very interest-
ing nonetheless. I would have
thought the method ideal for
secondhand tv shops where they
might buy up old TVs cheaply and
rejuvenate them for resale.

                      Brian.

Sometimes you can replace that background by some simple lines to help with the illusion of movement (like the pavement in MR NUMO in OUT- LET 100.

While testing, one can simply load the screens one by one from disk in a loop.

When you have your frames you need to compress them. I use the PICPACKER from OUTLET 35.

The compressed frames need to be all loaded into memory in sequ- ence and their start addresses noted. The whole lot are then resaved as one big block of code for convenience.

If you feel like having a go you can nick the BASIC from one of the previous animations as a template if you want. They're good fun but do take time and a lot of patience! Brian

From: Colin Bibby

10 LOAD "B:":SAVE"B:":LOAD"DISK"

In addition to the above I have only recently come up with the following which is a very rapid "B" autobooter....

In other words. Save the line 10 above on a spare 3" disc. An odd disc with faulty sectors should suit this job very well.

My new bit came from Page 72 in the +3 manual concerning DATA. I'm going to  keep this as brief as possible but do write through Outlet for further info if req..

Let's assume you want to gain access to a disc in the B drive containing just three programs.

These might be named "ONE" "TWO" and "THREE" My program to gain instant access to any of these programs would be wrote as follows:-

10 FOR a=1 TO 3 20 READ n$ 30 PRINT n$ 40 DATA "1 = ONE" , "2 = TWO" , "3 = THREE" 50 NEXT a 60 INPUT "ENTER CHOICE 1 TO 3",z 70 IF z=1 THEN LOAD "ONE" 80 IF z=2 THEN LOAD "TWO" 90 IF z=3 THEN LOAD "THREE"

To save the above onto any disc do remember to include the line number 10 for it to autoboot as follows:-

SAVE "DISK" LINE 10

Brian Cavers to Colin Bibby

First, I must point out that it is AN INFRINGEMENT OF COPYRIGHT to copy OUTLET disks and sell either the originals OR the copies! It is technically ill- egal to make ANY copies of OUT- LET but we permit readers to make copies for their own use such as for backup or onto a different system.

You should NEVER sell or even give away copies of OUTLET. The odd one to a friend as a sample to entice them to join is OK but should not be repeated.

It is OK to sell as secondhand ORIGINALS of OUTLET SO LONG AS YOU DO NOT KEEP COPIES.

I'm sure your intentions were innocent but if you think about it you can see how soon we would be out of business if everyone did it! We'd only need to sell one OUTLET a month and it could be passed around to everyone, each of whom could keep a copy! Of course, the next month there would be no OUTLETs at all!

We're well aware that we are ripped off left,right and centre and ultimately there is not much we can do about it but we are certainly not going to help by permitting adverts in OUTBOARD! I have therefore removed that part of your advert pertaining to OUTLETs and trust you will not sell them unless you first erase your copies.

I should add that MANY items in OUTLET are public domain or what we call FREEWARE. These individ- ual programs may be copied,sold, or given away to your heart's content! Items NOT so marked are copyright and must not be passed on or sold to others.

Regarding the FILECARD program, your comment that"I'm sure Chez- ron will be pleased to distrib- ute this program to anyone on request" implies that we will just send a copy to anyone for free! Sorry! Anyone wanting the program must buy OUTLET 48. Yes, I know how mercenary it sounds but although OUTLET makes no profit now we do need to cover all sorts of costs to keep it going.

Plus 3 DOS does not provide a single 'current drive' feature like the Plus D or Disciple but splits it between 'current drive for reading' and 'current drive for writing'.The SAVE "B:"that I recommended makes sure that B is current for writing too. If you want to be sure all programs will work fully on Drive B - and exclusively on B - then you need the SAVE "B:". Otherwise,a prog- ram saving data may unexpectedly save to Drive A. That might be what you want in some cases but in general if you want to switch to using B as the current drive you need both LOAD "B:" and SAVE "B:". Brian.

From: Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

Dear Brian,

I read your letter about tube ageing, and thought I might be able to throw a little light on the problem (no pun intended). The symptoms of low brightness and poor focus are caused by the gradual build-up of impurities on the cathode, and it is this which reduces its ability to emit electrons.

A partial cure can be to run the tube heaters for several minutes at a higher than normal voltage, as the increased temperature then 'boils off' some of the contaminants, exposing a fresh layer of emissive material.

This can give a temporary new lease of life to a tube that is on its 'last legs', but needs to be carried out under very strict conditions to avoid unnecessary strain on the heaters.

In the earlier days of televis- ion servicing, this technique used to be fairly common, as it was cost-effective to defer the (considerable) expense of tube replacement. Nowadays, however, it's probably more economical to buy a new set, so I don't know if the practice is still as widespread.

I came across a servicing manual (Newnes TV & Video Engineers' Pocket Book) that describes the

tube rejuvenation process more fully: while over-running the heaters for several seconds, a positive voltage should also be applied to the grid, to attract the oxides away from the cathode.

Best wishes,

Miles Kinloch

Brian Cavers to Miles Kinloch

Many thanks, Miles. Too advanced for me to try but very interest- ing nonetheless. I would have thought the method ideal for secondhand tv shops where they might buy up old TVs cheaply and rejuvenate them for resale.

Brian.

**Brian Cavers отвечает Arnold Yates:**

Что это за программа — Icon Graphic 128? Мне такое название неизвестно. Если это графический/текстовый редактор, возможно, вам лучше подойдет WORDMASTER.

Дизассемблировать и изменять машинный код — дело непростое. Нельзя просто взять дизассемблер, выучить пару правил и сразу браться за дело. Это намного сложнее, чем править BASIC, что само по себе временами бывает очень нелегко. Кроме того, изменить описываемую вами программу может оказаться непросто или даже невозможно — в зависимости от того, как именно она формирует 32-колоночный вывод. Возможно, перенаправить вывод на полноразмерный принтер еще реально, но изменить ширину — гораздо сложнее. Программа может печатать определяемую графику Sinclair на ZX printer, но для эмуляции этого на полноразмерном принтере потребуется полностью переписать код.

**Brian Cavers отвечает Colin Bibby:**

Дорожки на двухстороннем диске могут форматироваться и нумероваться последовательно от начала стороны A до конца стороны A, а затем от начала стороны B до конца стороны B. Это метод «SUCCESSIVE SIDES» (последовательные стороны).

Либо диск можно форматировать иначе: дорожка 0 на стороне A, затем дорожка 0 на стороне B, потом дорожка 1 на стороне A, затем дорожка 1 на стороне B и так далее до последних дорожек на каждой стороне. Это метод «ALTERNATE SIDES» (чередующиеся стороны). У дисковода две головки — по одной с каждой стороны, поэтому ему не нужно физически перемещаться туда-обратно между сторонами.

Какой способ лучше? Сомневаюсь, что есть какая-то существенная разница, так что не переживайте и просто соглашайтесь со значением по умолчанию (если только кто-то не знает наверняка).

Количество записей в каталоге — другое дело. Если вы выберете 256, вы сможете сохранить на диске больше файлов (фактически на 128 больше!), но общий объем диска немного уменьшится (706K). Это удобно для дисков, где вы хотите хранить максимальное количество очень маленьких файлов, скажем, около 200 текстовых файлов по 2K. Но если 128 файлов среднего размера вам более чем достаточно, то имеет смысл получить дополнительные 4K свободного места и отформатировать диск на 710K.

Brian

Дорогие читатели Outlet!

Хочу сообщить всем вам, что недавно я приобрела оцифровщик Romantic Robot Digitiser.

**Brian отвечает Bernadette Dowsland:**

Я годами мечтал об одном из таких оцифровщиков, но для Spectrum так и не достал. Позже я купил плату видеозахвата для PC и могу использовать ее и для Spectrum, преобразуя картинку в черно-белую и перенося файлы. Именно так я делаю анимации, которые иногда вставляю в OUTLET.

С дигитайзером можно отлично развлечься, особенно делая анимацию. Чтобы сделать анимацию, вам нужно какое-то циклическое движение, чтобы оно повторялось: например, Bugs Bunny, за которым гонится Yosemite Sam. Важно, чтобы цикл укладывался не более чем, скажем, в 8–12 кадров (в зависимости от сложности).

Также важно, чтобы последний кадр «стыковался» с первым для создания зацикленного ряда кадров. Часто приходится дорабатывать кадры вручную в графическом редакторе. Это может быть очень трудоемким процессом!

Например, ноги и руки Yosemite Sam, бегущего за Bugs Bunny, могут идеально переходить из финального кадра в первый, но фон может внезапно дернуться, сменившись другой сценой, поэтому его приходится стирать вручную точка за точкой, оставляя только фигуры. Иногда этот фон можно заменить простыми линиями, помогающими создать иллюзию движения (как тротуар в «MR NUMO» в OUTLET 100).

Во время тестирования экраны можно просто загружать по очереди с диска в цикле.

Когда кадры готовы, их нужно сжать. Я использую PICPACKER из OUTLET 35.

Сжатые кадры нужно загрузить в память один за другим и записать их начальные адреса. Затем для удобства все это заново сохраняется в виде одного большого блока кода.

Если хотите попробовать, можете стянуть BASIC из одной из предыдущих анимаций в качестве шаблона. Это очень увлекательно, но требует времени и огромного терпения!

Brian

Моя новая идея пришла со страницы 72 руководства к +3, касающейся DATA. Постараюсь изложить как можно короче, но пишите в Outlet, если потребуется дополнительная информация.

Предположим, вы хотите получить доступ к диску в дисководе B, содержащему всего три программы.

Они могут называться «ONE», «TWO» и «THREE». Моя программа для мгновенного доступа к любой из них пишется следующим образом:

```text
10 FOR a=1 TO 3
20 READ n$
30 PRINT n$
40 DATA "1 = ONE" , "2 = TWO" , "3 = THREE"
50 NEXT a
60 INPUT "ENTER CHOICE 1 TO 3",z
70 IF z=1 THEN LOAD "ONE"
80 IF z=2 THEN LOAD "TWO"
90 IF z=3 THEN LOAD "THREE"
```

Чтобы сохранить вышеуказанное на любой диск, не забудьте указать номер строки 10 для автозапуска:

```text
SAVE "DISK" LINE 10
```

Указание LINE 10 избавит от необходимости набирать RUN после загрузки.

Несомненно, уже существует множество программ, предлагающих подобный функционал, но все же есть особое очарование в том, чтобы время от времени написать что-то свое, заточенное под индивидуальные нужды.

Plus 3 DOS не имеет понятия единого «текущего дисковода», как Plus D или Disciple, а разделяет его на «текущий дисковод для чтения» и «текущий дисковод для записи». Команда SAVE "B:", которую я рекомендовал, гарантирует, что диск B станет текущим и для записи тоже. Если вы хотите быть уверены, что все программы будут полноценно работать на дисководе B — и исключительно на B, — вам необходима SAVE "B:". В противном случае программа, сохраняющая данные, может неожиданно произвести запись на дисковод A. В некоторых случаях это может быть именно то, что нужно, но в целом, если вы хотите переключиться на использование B в качестве текущего дисковода, вам нужны как LOAD "B:", так и SAVE "B:".

Brian.

Частичным решением проблемы может стать прогрев накала трубки в течение нескольких минут при напряжении выше номинального, поскольку повышенная температура «выпаривает» часть загрязнений, обнажая свежий слой эмиссионного материала.

Это может временно вдохнуть новую жизнь в трубку, которая уже «дышит на ладан», но процедуру нужно проводить в строго определенных условиях, чтобы избежать чрезмерной нагрузки на нити накала.

В былые времена обслуживания телевизоров этот метод был довольно распространен, поскольку было экономически выгодно отложить (весьма немалые) расходы на замену кинескопа.
